correctness.rationale: For any pair of competitors, equality of their relative reproduction odds forces equality of susceptibility-weighted neighbor payoffs. The all-cooperative configuration with unequal positive benefit/cost forces same susceptibilities for every common-neighbor pair. Varying cost and binary basis strategy configurations then forces identical simple-random-walk rows on any common-neighbor component carrying nonzero susceptibility. The common-neighbor auxiliary graph is connected on a connected nonbipartite graph and has the two sides as components on a connected bipartite graph. An active component of identical rows yields precisely complete bipartite graph structure. Conversely, side-constant susceptibilities cancel as a common multiplicative fitness factor at each vacancy. Verified exact rational finite diagnostics, including 180099 graph-profile cases and every connected simple graph through six vertices; those computations supplement, not replace, the proof. Delta=0 and single-neighbor competitions handled explicitly.

originality.rationale: The source introduces exponential comparison fitness and weak-selection coalescent consequences, but the accessible full main paper neither characterizes individual update cancellation at arbitrary strength nor proves an iff graph/profile classification. Full text comparison with Peña–Rochat (2012) and Szolnoki–Perc (2021) found different interaction/replacement schemes or imitation averaging. Published research-index searches for graph twins, gauge invariance, complete bipartite microscopic invisibility, and exact parameter nullspaces did not reveal a covering claim; failure of search is not novelty proof. An unexamined separate supplemental source remains a risk.
residual_risks: Separately hosted supplementary material of arXiv:2609.39012v1 was not materially available; it may contain a special-case invariance observation, though the main paper does not assert a general iff classification.

The selected equivalence is at the microscopic individual replacement-probability level, which is stronger than and not interchangeable with equality of aggregate strategy-state transitions.

value.rationale: This is an exact nonidentifiability classification for a natural newly introduced evolutionary cooperation model, not a routine graph count. It locates the maximal invisible susceptibility subspace (two side constants) on complete bipartite graphs and proves no nonzero profile can be invisible on any other connected simple graph. As a consequence, arbitrary positive selection and arbitrarily large heterogeneous social-comparison strengths can leave the entire strategic Markov law unchanged on stars and bicliques. It supplies sharp structural control cases for interpreting network influence and estimating behavioral parameters; one cannot infer all susceptibility parameters from such trajectories.
